newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAILAND SAYS NO CHANGE IN VAT TAX HIKE PLAN.
newsitem.headline: THAILAND SAYS NO CHANGE IN VAT TAX HIKE PLAN.

text.p: Thai finance minister Thanong Bidaya said on Wednesday the government would stick to its decision to raise the value added tax (VAT) to 10 percent from seven percent from August 16 despite strong public criticism of the plan.

Thanong told a radio station the tax hike would be Thailand's signal to the world community that its people are prepared to face austerity measures after the country obtained a $16 billion loan package from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and other nations to revive its battered economy.

"I have been assured by the prime minister that national survival must come first...we have built up a lot of debts in the past four to five years. How could we explain to other countries that we seek their financial help while we still do not stop our excessive spending," he said.

Thanong said Thailand will start tapping loans from the $16 billion package, including $4 billion contributed by the IMF, when its foreign reserves fall below a level sufficient for financing four months of imports.
The opposition has called on the government to review the VAT hike plan, saying it could be avoided if Chavalit's six-party coalition agreed to cut more of its 1997/1998 (October-September) budget.
Chavalit's cabinet has agreed to slash 50-75 billion baht ($1.6-$2.3 billion) from Thailand's 982 billion baht budget for 1997/98. It will decide on details of ministerial spending cuts next week.
